content.comment_body: In [version_no], I can choose between different Ethernet adapters on my PC, including those built into the motherboard and connected via USB-C. In [version_no], however, all options except the motherboard NIC are greyed out. I am running both versions with administrator privileges. Is there a setting I might have overlooked? Regards, [user_name]
It’s possible that something went wrong during installation. Which operating system are you using?
I am using Datacenter 2022. Both versions are installed on the same computer. [version_no] allows me to choose adapters, while [version_no] does not.
Is it possible that [version_no] is running in demo mode? How can I check for this?
Do you have a full version installed, or is it a demo version? With a demo, communication functions—including selection of Ethernet adapters—may not be available in [product_name].
I have a full version of [version_no] installed from CD, and I downloaded an upgrade to [version_no]. Now both versions are installed on the machine.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that the newer version of [product_name] limits Ethernet adapter selection to the onboard network card, in contrast to the previous version where all adapters were accessible. This reduces workflow flexibility for those needing different network interfaces. The unclear distinction between demo and full versions adds to troubleshooting difficulties.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to select any Ethernet adapter in [version_no], just as they could in [version_no]. There is also an expectation for consistent functionality and clearer communication regarding feature availability between software releases.
